answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
**Can I go back to 40 miles next week?** No. Forty miles is more than three times last week's 12, and that jump would load legs that are still recovering. Next week is about 16 miles, all easy.

**Can I start speedwork for the 10K?** Not yet. Faster running can wait until easy runs feel normal and your quads are no longer sore, which is likely three or more weeks away. The Thanksgiving 10K is about four weeks out, so it is only a realistic target if your legs come around by early November. I would make that call at your next check-in.

**What comes next?** Tell me which race you want next, its date, and whether the Thanksgiving 10K is still on, so I can build toward it.

new.analysis:
Last week matched the plan on every day. The three easy runs came in at 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0 miles, and the other four days were rest, so nothing was skipped or overrun. The heart rate stayed in the easy zones on every run.

The race was the heavy load of the block. You finished about 3:50 on your watch, five minutes off your under 3:45 target, and the last 10K slowed. Your legs were back by Thursday, which is a good sign, but a marathon usually needs more time than a few easy days before the body is fully back to normal training.

| Week | Miles run | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 5 – 11 | 34.0 | Build week before the race |
| Oct 12 – 18 | 41.2 | Race week, including the 26.2 mile marathon |
| Oct 19 – 25 | 12.0 | Easy recovery, all done as planned |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | 16.0 | Easy only, no quality sessions |

Going from 12 miles to 40 would more than triple the load in one step. Adding volume gradually keeps fatigue from building back up after the race, so next week is about a third more than last week. Two rest days and one walk or bike keep the week light while the legs settle.

Speedwork would add hard running on legs that are still recovering. Quality sessions should come back only after easy running feels normal, and that is the trigger I will use before adding any faster work. Your slower easy pace fits recovery rather than lost fitness, so judge the runs by heart rate and how they feel this week.
